justification: Adds an outbound side effect to a live API route. The route already committed the submitter's feedback before this runs, so every failure path in the new code has to be swallowed or a mail outage becomes a 500 on a submission that was already saved.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: The alert stops carrying the complaint text, the cohort tag, or the missing-contact marker; or notifyOperator stops swallowing a Resend constructor throw, a rejected send, or an absent API key.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Three separate mutations, each killing exactly one test and leaving nine passing: swallow removed -> 1 failed/9 passed; cohort tag dropped from the subject -> 1 failed/9 passed; missing-contact marker silenced -> 1 failed/9 passed. Baseline and restored both 10 passed.

pre_impl.existing_data: user_feedback, written by this route. The widget already collects type, severity, user role, property address, section, free text, an optional submitter contact address and a cohort/class code in context_data. All of it was already stored; none of it was ever announced.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The route has an `email` field and it looks like a notification address. It is not - it is the SUBMITTER's `contact_email`. Nothing in the repo watched the table, and no scheduled digest existed. The gap was invisible precisely because the field that would carry an alert already had a plausible-looking value in it.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to new submissions only. Existing rows are not replayed - anything already in user_feedback stays unannounced and must be read directly.

functions.name: buildFeedbackAlert
functions.input: FeedbackAlertFields: the row id, feedbackType, severity, userType, address, section, the free-text complaint, contactEmail (nullable) and cohort (nullable).
functions.output: { subject, text }. Subject is `Feedback[<cohort>]: <type> - <address>`, with the bracketed tag omitted entirely when cohort is null. Text is the metadata block, a blank line, the complaint verbatim, and the row id.
functions.if_none: It cannot receive nothing - it is only called after a successful insert, so id and the required strings exist. The two nullable fields each have an explicit rendering: a null cohort drops both the subject tag and the body line, and a null contactEmail renders '(no contact address)' rather than interpolating undefined.
functions.why: Pure message construction, split from the sender so the wording is testable without sending anything.

functions.name: notifyOperator
functions.input: The same FeedbackAlertFields, plus process.env.RESEND_API_KEY and process.env.NOTIFY_EMAIL read at call time.
functions.output: boolean - whether a send was DISPATCHED. Not whether it was delivered, which it cannot know: the send is not awaited, and the Workspace self-domain quarantine fails after Resend has reported success. The caller ignores the result; it exists so the outcome is inspectable and each failure path says which one it took.
functions.if_none: No RESEND_API_KEY returns false without sending. A throwing Resend constructor is caught and returns false. A rejecting send still returns true, because dispatch already happened and is the most the function can honestly claim. All three are silent to the submitter by design - the feedback row committed before this ran.
functions.why: The sender. Every failure path is swallowed so a mail problem cannot turn a saved submission into a 500.

values.name: NOTIFY_EMAIL
values.read_at: Module load of frontend-nextjs/app/api/feedback/route.ts, from the process environment. Same constant, same default and same reasoning as the six existing routes that already notify.
values.if_missing: Falls back to the hardcoded off-domain gmail address, so the alert still arrives rather than silently going nowhere. A test asserts the recipient never ends in @plotdetect.com.au.
values.why: Must NOT be @plotdetect.com.au. Sending from info@plotdetect.com.au to the same domain via Resend is quarantined by Google Workspace as self-domain spoofing - Resend reports 'delivered' and it never arrives.

break_it.scenario: Resend is down, rate-limited, or the API key is malformed when someone submits feedback.
break_it.what_happens: Without swallowing, the throw propagates out of the POST handler and the submitter gets 'Failed to save feedback' - for feedback that was already committed to the database one line earlier. They would likely resubmit, duplicating the row, or give up.
break_it.how: notifyOperator returns early with no key, wraps the constructor in try/catch, and attaches .catch to the send promise. It is called after the insert has succeeded and its result is not awaited.
break_it.repro: Replace the catch body with `throw err;` -> 1 failed, 9 passed

break_it.scenario: An alert arrives saying only that feedback exists.
break_it.what_happens: Every alert then costs a database round trip to action, which is the same delay the change exists to remove. The operator learns to ignore them.
break_it.how: The body carries the complaint text, the address, the section, the severity and the submitter's contact address; the subject carries the type and address.
break_it.repro: Drop `fields.text` from the body -> the 'carries the actual complaint' test fails

break_it.scenario: A whole class submits feedback and it cannot be told apart from public traffic.
break_it.what_happens: Cohort feedback is the entire point of the class-code link. Without the tag in the subject it cannot be filtered or grouped in an inbox, so a teaching-period trial produces an undifferentiated pile.
break_it.how: The cohort is read from context and rendered as a bracketed subject tag plus a body line, and omitted entirely when absent so public feedback carries no empty marker.
break_it.repro: Remove ${cohortTag} from the subject -> 1 failed, 9 passed

break_it.scenario: The submitter left no contact address.
break_it.what_happens: Naive interpolation renders 'undefined' where an address belongs, which reads as a broken address rather than an absent one, and invites a reply to nobody.
break_it.how: Renders '(no contact address)' explicitly; a test asserts the string 'undefined' never appears.
break_it.repro: Replace the marker with an empty string -> 1 failed, 9 passed

break_it.scenario: The notifier reports success it cannot actually know.
break_it.what_happens: The send is not awaited and Workspace quarantines a same-domain send AFTER Resend reports delivered. A function claiming 'sent' would be asserting something unobservable, and the tests would enshrine it.
break_it.how: The return value means DISPATCHED, not delivered, and both the docstring and the test name say so. A rejected send still returns true because dispatch did occur; only an absent key or a throwing constructor return false.
break_it.repro: The 'reports true when the send is dispatched, even if it later rejects' test pins this distinction

post_merge.secrets: No - RESEND_API_KEY and NOTIFY_EMAIL already exist in the environment for the six routes that already notify.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - submit one piece of feedback through the live widget and confirm the alert arrives. The self-domain quarantine failure mode reports success at the API and still never delivers, so an end-to-end send is the only way to know.
